KEY MESSAGE 1..Southerly onshore flow and a mix of high clouds and 
diurnal Cu will be the name of the game this afternoon as high 
pressure continues to shift further offshore. This mornings upper 
air sounding still shows pretty widespread dry air across ENC today 
so outside of some increasing cloud cover as moisture continues to 
advect in moistening up the atm profile, not expecting much in 
the way of rain this afternoon. Highs get into the low 90s to 
upper 80s inland and mid 80s along the coast and OBX today. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...We enter into an unsettled pattern once again 
starting tonight into Sunday with daily chances for showers and 
thunderstorms into at least mid week. Upper level trough currently 
in the Midwest will dive SE'wards into the Tennessee River Valley 
Sun into Mon eventually stalling as an upper level ridge blocks
this troughs forward progress. At the mid levels, will see 
multiple shortwaves round the base of this trough promoting 
periods of lift across ENC and the offshore waters with the 
first weak mid level shortwave tracking along the coast starting
tonight into Sun morning with additional shortwaves coming in 
from the west Sun afternoon and again on Mon/Tue. At the 
surface, closed low in the Midwest will gradually shift E'wards 
into the Ohio River Valley with its associated surface front 
stalling just to the west. These features, in addition to the 
sea breeze each afternoon/evening, will be the main forcing 
present for a notable increase in precip chances. 

Starting later tonight into Sun there will be two areas of 
focus for shower and thunderstorm activity. The first will be 
overnight into Sun morning along and behind a N'ward moving warm
front/coastal trough with much of the activity occuring near 
and east of Hwy 17. We should still be too dry aloft inland as 
the boundary moves through, so thunder chances remain low inland
Sun morning. Proximity to the gulf stream could allow isolated 
to scattered showers and thunderstorms to reach coastal 
communities south of Oregon Inlet. The second will be in the 
afternoon/evening with shower and thunderstorm activity coming 
in from the west associated with the stalling upper trough. 
Cloud cover will play a big role in how high instability can 
truly get, but with the dewpoints rising there should be enough 
instability entering the region for 1000-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE 
Sunday. While shear is not too impressive with the 
unidirectional SE flow, the combination of long, skinny CAPEs, 
PWATs over 2", and slow storm motions could result in heavy 
rainfall rates and wet microbursts where storms develop. The 
best coverage is expected to be to our west closer to I-95, with
more isolated to scattered coverage across the Coastal Plain 
but will continue to monitor trends in the CAM guidance and 
adjust PoPs accordingly. 

Monday the trough will remain stalled to our west and gradually 
weaken. This reduces the potential for height falls over the region 
despite the trough creeping a bit closer. Still, we should see 
embedded shortwaves moving through aloft. Slightly better 
forcing, paired with another day of long skinny CAPEs and PWATs 
north of 2" brings higher precip chances compared to Sunday with
heavy rainfall rates, a low end wet microburst threat, and slow
storm motion vectors. All this brings flash flooding concerns 
to mind, especially with how much rain has been observed in many
locations in the past 1-2 weeks.

We are currently in a Marginal (level 1/5) Excessive Rain Outlook 
for Sunday and Monday with best chances at seeing flash flooding
likely along Hwy 17 and points east. What prevents it from 
being higher is the uncertainty on instability with antecedent 
cloud cover and the lack of substantial ground-level forcing. 
With high temps forecast to only be in the low to mid 80s 
Monday, the sea breeze may be weak in nature. 

Beyond Monday, the trough/low is still expected to linger to our 
west until eventually it gets picked up and shifted to our north by 
another trough moving through the Great Lakes region. As a result, 
daily elevated precip chances continue through mid-week with a low 
end risk for flash flooding. By the end of the week it looks like we 
return back to climo or below climo PoPs as a lack of mid level 
shortwaves or significant forcing will be noted across ENC though we 
do begin to warm back up with temps returning to the upper 80s to 
low 90s inland and mid 80s along the OBX.
